Antropi Robotics (YC F26) is building autonomous factories that make inspected CNC parts for hardware teams in days instead of weeks. CNC machines already cut metal automatically, but people still need to plan jobs, load machines, inspect parts, and handle problems. Antropi’s Factory OS connects these steps into one system. Its first factory is live and already shipping parts to customers with lead times under 7 days. The goal is a network of autonomous factories across the US that make and deliver parts locally in as little as 24 hours. Founders Naman Gupta and Shubh Agarwal have been building hardware together since college in 2017. Naman was the first employee and Chief of Staff at Accio Robotics before running his dad’s CNC machining business. Shubh completed his Master’s in Robotics at the University of Pennsylvania, working with robotic manipulators. [Button: …more ]

Another Rize for YC success story! 🚀 Huge congratulations to Naman Gupta and Shubh Agarwal, co-founders of Antropi Robotics, for making it into the YC Fall 2026 batch! Antropi is building autonomous factories for the physical world - factories that run 24/7, where software and robots turn raw metal into finished parts with almost no human intervention. Their vision: make manufacturing as programmable as software, so you ask for a part, and the factory makes it. They're building the infrastructure to produce the next frontier of technology: hardware. Rize community is proud to have supported Naman and Shubh on this journey. From a bold idea to a YC-backed company, this is exactly the kind of ambition we love backing! 🚀

Antropi Robotics is joining Y Combinator (F26). We build autonomous CNC factories. Most factories today still run on manual effort. Machines wait on people, quality gets checked at the end, and even simple parts take weeks. We envision factories built on physical AI, where software, robots, and CNC machines work as one system: it plans the job, machines the part, inspects it, and corrects itself.
